narrative: Material PL1__M39D7511 exhibits high-variability demand (CV=0.558) with a silent zero-demand period in early observations, followed by active consumption averaging 477 units/day. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.619, mean 1.41 days), with transport variability contributing 63.5% of total buffer requirement. The recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy sets safety stock at 863 units (z=1.645 * sigma_LTD=524.6) and an EOQ order quantity of 3,066 units, reducing annual orders from ~1,074 to ~39 while holding costs remain manageable at ~$3,035/year against $1,950 in ordering costs.
warnings: Zero-demand period detected in first 22 working days — may indicate ramp-up or data gap; excluded from active demand statistics
Lead time CV=0.619 classified as unstable — monitor supplier/transport reliability closely
Safety lead time reduced from SAP value of 3.0 days to empirically-derived 1.81 days

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-variability but mostly continuous demand (85.6% non-zero days) suits a continuous-review reorder-point system. EOQ balances the large fixed ordering cost ($50) against relatively low unit holding cost ($1.27/unit/year), yielding large infrequent orders. Safety stock is calibrated analytically using the combined demand-and-lead-time variance formula at z=1.645 for 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 7,218 units is not binding: peak inventory (SS 863 + OQ 3,066 = 3,929 units) uses only 54% of available space, leaving comfortable headroom. No capacity-driven order quantity reduction was required.
